intro: The {languages.count} languages documented here — {languages.list} — are spoken on Gaua Island (Banks Islands, Vanuatu), distributed from east to west.

cards.grammar: A systematic comparative description of grammatical structures across all {languages.count} Gaua languages. Every claim is illustrated with interlinear glossed examples; every morpheme links to the dictionary.
cards.texts: A curated index of natural language texts — myths, procedural texts, narratives, and ritual speech — each linking directly to its archived item in the LACITO Pangloss Collection.
cards.dictionary: A comparative lexicon giving each form across all {languages.count} languages, with part of speech, semantic gloss, usage notes, and bidirectional links to the glossed grammatical examples.

map.title: The Island of Gaua
text: Gaua (once charted as Santa Maria) is a volcanic island in the Banks Islands group of northern Vanuatu, in the south-western Pacific. It rises to 797 m at Mt Garet, whose crater contains Lake Letas, the largest lake in Vanuatu. The island's population of roughly 2,500 people is distributed across coastal villages speaking six distinct languages. Five of them — Nume, Dorig, Koro, Olrat, and Lakon — are documented in this Digital Boasian Trilogy. A sixth language, Mwerlap, is spoken in the south-east of the island and is not included here.

The five DBT languages form a genealogically and geographically coherent dialect chain, distributed from east (Nume, ~700 speakers) to west (Lakon, ~800 speakers), with Olrat occupying a small enclave near Jōlav with only ~3 remaining fluent speakers — making it one of the most critically endangered languages of the Pacific.
